## Using R via Command Line and Scripts

## 1. Accessing the R console

Open a terminal (Command Prompt on Windows, Terminal on Mac/Linux) and type:

```{bash}
#| eval: false
R
```
This launches the R console, where you can type and execute R commands interactively.

::: {#fig-r-terminal}
![](./images/r_terminal.png)

R console in a terminal.
:::

## 2. Creating an R Script

Open your preferred text editor (e.g. [VS Code for mac](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/?dv=osx), Notepad, [Notepad++ for Windows](https://notepad-plus-plus.org/downloads/), Rstudio). 

Write your R code and save file with a .R extension. 

## 3. Executing the R script in the Terminal

Navigate to the directory where your script is saved:

```{bash}
#| eval: false
cd path/to/your/folder
```

Replace `path/to/your/folder` with the actual path where your script.R is saved.

- On Windows, paths might look like `C:\Users\YourName\Documents\Rscripts`

- On Mac/Linux, paths might look like `/Users/YourName/Documents/Rscripts`

```{bash}
#| eval: false
Rscript script.R
```



## 4. Using R with Rgui

Rgui is a program that is installed alongside R when you install it. It is the
standard R user interface. But nobody uses it...

::: {#fig-r-rgui}
![](./images/r_gui.png)

R GUI on macOS.
:::

## Using R with RStudio - Our focus in this course

RStudio is an integrated development environment (IDE) designed primarily for
running R code. It adds many more features and tools to R that allow us to
create, e.g.: 

- reproducible data analyses (via Rmarkdown/Quarto);
- interactive dashboarding tools (via RShiny).

It is now possible to run Python code, C++ code, SQL queries, ... directly from RStudio.

### Shortcuts

Some useful keyboard shortcuts:

-   Run current line/selection: Ctrl + Enter (⌘ + ⏎)

-   Insert assignment operator: Alt + − (⎇ + −)

-   Insert pipe operator: Ctrl + Shift + M (⌘ + ⇧ + M)

To see all the shortcuts and modify them:

<center><code>Tools -\> Modify Keyboard Shortcuts...</code></center>
